text:
anya: saw a regression on streaming tail latency starting ~03:40 UTC after last runtime rollout. chunk cadence jitter increased, a bunch of stream stalls. attaching quick logs and a few traces. :frowning:

samir: ugh. is this across all routes or just the heavy ones? any kernel change in the rollout?

mike: looks per-route. high qps routes with longer context are hit worse. I pulled the node-level spans — server-side scheduling time jumps by ~8-12ms on those tokens. client ack times stable.

anya: here's a snippet from the probe traces: 
```
stream-id=abc123 node=runtime-12 event=emit chunk_n=7 server_schedule_ms=15 client_ack_ms=2 kernel=auto_select(v3_quant)
stream-id=abc123 node=runtime-12 event=emit chunk_n=8 server_schedule_ms=28 client_ack_ms=3 kernel=auto_select(v3_quant)
stream-id=abc123 node=runtime-12 event=stall chunk_n=9 server_schedule_ms=200 client_ack_ms=2 kernel=aten_fused
```

claire: interesting — kernel switched around the same time we flipped the new kernel-selector heuristic (change 7782). It prefers fused aten kernels on medium batch sizes; maybe it misrouted some variable-length batches and caused backend scheduling thrash.

dmitri: also seeing a KV cache churn spike correlated at 03:41. evictions/sec up 4x for that pool. eviction log shows TTL-based clears + size bump. if cache misses spike, we regen KV and cost looks like extra blocking on the scheduler.

perf-bot: ALERT: stream_stall_rate for route /v1/generate exceeded threshold (2.1% > 1.0%) at 2163001240. Incident ID: PB-20260318-07.

mike: quick PromQL checks I ran: 
```
avg_over_time(stream_server_schedule_ms{route="/v1/generate"}[5m]) by (node)
rate(kv_evictions_total{pool="shared-24"}[5m])
```
node runtime-12 shows the biggest bump.

samir: can we confirm kernel-selector logs? add verbose for auto_select and dump the selection input (seq_len histogram + batch size) for the next 10m. also pin node runtime-12 to previous kernel until we triage.

claire: will push a small patch to the selector heuristics: fall back to scalar aten when seq_len variance > 0.35 OR if kv_evictions/sec > 100. patch will be a hot config change, no rebuild. rolling it to a canary now.

anya: thanks. also we should add a token-level latency breakdown panel (server schedule, kernel exec, kv wait, network) for per-route KPIs on the streaming dashboard so we can correlate without digging raw traces. mike can you sketch queries?

mike: yep. prototypes: 
- server_schedule_ms: histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(stream_server_schedule_bucket[5m])) by (le, route))
- kernel_exec_ms: sum(rate(kernel_exec_seconds_count[5m])) by (route) / sum(rate(kernel_exec_seconds_sum[5m])) by (route)  # avg exec
- kv_wait_ms: increase(kv_wait_ms_sum[5m]) / increase(kv_wait_ms_count[5m])
I'll add panels: per-route 95p token latency stack and per-node kernel-choice heatmap.

dmitri: for KV immediate mitigation I suggested bumping pool size TTL from 600->1200s and temporarily disable aggressive background compaction. will monitor evictions.

anya: canary looks better so far for route /v1/generate — early numbers show stream_stall_rate down to 0.8% on runtime-12. keep monitoring for 15m then we can promote.

samir: approved promote if stable. also open a follow-up ticket to add automated alerts when kernel_selector flips >5% across healthy nodes in 1m window. too noisy today.

mike: pushed dashboard PR with panels + queries, linking in the ticket.

claire: patch promoted to all nodes at 2163001289. will keep verbose selector logging for 30m.

anya: nice work team :tada: please drop any interesting selector traces here. will close the incident if metrics stay flat for 30m.

mike: adding a couple of sample traces to the ticket.

dmitri: KV evictions dropped to baseline after TTL bump.

perf-bot: INCIDENT RESOLVED: PB-20260318-07 at 2163001350.

anya: closing thread once we confirm 30m stable. :eyes:
